Prevent creation, reading, updating, and deletion of records from other scopes

pergunta: Which is an example of when an application might use a Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job)?

alternativas.texto: The application needs to run a client-side script at the same time every day.
alternativas.explicacao:
A Scheduled Script Execution (Scheduled Job) in ServiceNow is used to run server-side logic on a time-based schedule (daily, weekly, monthly,...).

A common example is automating background tasks such as checking for records, sending reminders, or performing clean-up activities.

Main knowledge to remember

Scheduled Jobs = Server-side automation, run on a schedule (query/update/send emails).

Client scripts/UI policies = Run in the browser for user interactions.

Business rules = Run on the server but triggered by database operations, not time.

Reference: Scheduled jobs (ServiceNow Docs)

pergunta: What field type would you select if you want to query records from another table on a form?

alternativas.explicacao:
If you want to query records from another table and display them on a form, you use the Reference field type. A reference field creates a relationship between the current table and another table by storing the sys_id of a record in the target table.

On the form, it displays as a field where you can search and select values from that related table.

Main knowledge to remember

Reference field = Points to records in another table (links by sys_id).

Used to create relationships like "Caller" (reference to sys_user) on the Incident table.

Other field types (Date, String, Phone) store simple data, not record references.

Reference: Reference field type (ServiceNow Docs)

pergunta: What happens to the List view when a new field is added to an existing table?

alternativas.texto: The new field is added at the start of the List
alternativas.explicacao:
When you add a new field to an existing table in ServiceNow, the field becomes part of the table schema, but it is not automatically displayed in existing list views.

To display the new field in a list, an administrator or user with the appropriate permissions must personalize the list or modify the List Layout to include the field.

The correct answer option(s): The new field is not added to the List view.

Adding a field updates the table definition.

Existing list layouts remain unchanged.

The field must be manually added to the list layout if you want it to appear.

Reference: Configure the list layout (ServiceNow Docs)

pergunta: Which options are strategies for debugging client-side scripts? (Choose two.)

alternativas.explicacao:
When debugging client-side scripts (scripts that run in the user’s browser like Client Scripts or UI Policies), you only have access to browser-side tools and APIs such as g_form and jslog().

✅ g_form.addInfoMessage() → Displays a message directly on the form.
Useful for checking variable values or script behavior visually on the UI.

✅ jslog() → Sends log output to the browser console.
Excellent for debugging since you can check logs in real-time using browser developer tools (F12 → Console).

Incorrect options:

gs.addErrorMessage() → Used in server-side scripts (Business Rules, Script Includes). Not available on the client side.

gs.log() → Also server-side only; writes messages to system logs, not the browser console.

Summary:

Client-side debugging → g_form.addInfoMessage() and jslog()

Server-side debugging → gs.addErrorMessage() and gs.log()

pergunta: Which of the following objects does a Before Business Rule have access to in a script?

alternativas.explicacao:
In ServiceNow, a Before Business Rule runs after a user submits a form but before the data is actually committed to the database. Because of this specific timing, the script has access to several powerful global objects to validate or modify data.

1. Current

The current object is a GlideRecord that contains the record as it exists in the buffer, including the changes made by the user on the form.

Usage: You use current to modify field values before they are saved.

Example:

current.short_description = "Updated by BR: " + current.short_description;

2. Previous

The previous object is a read-only GlideRecord containing the values of the record exactly as they exist in the database before the current update.

Usage: It is primarily used for comparison logic to see if a specific field was changed.

Example:

if (current.assignment_group != previous.assignment_group) { // do something }

3. GlideRecord

The GlideRecord API is the standard way to interact with the ServiceNow database. While current and previous are specific instances of a GlideRecord, you can also initialize new GlideRecord objects within your script to look up data in other tables.

Usage: Querying related records or performing validation against different tables.

Example:

var gr = new GlideRecord('sys_user');

Reference: Abort a database action (ServiceNow Docs)

pergunta:
Exportitem table is extended from Item Table with the additional column of ItemCountry added. The Item table contains the columns ItemName and ItemQty.

Which fields are available in the ExportItem Table?

alternativas.explicacao:
In ServiceNow, when a table is extended from another table, it inherits all fields and functionality from its parent table.
This means that the ExportItem table automatically includes all columns from the Item table, plus any additional fields defined on itself.

So:

Parent Table (Item) → has ItemName, ItemQty.

Child Table (ExportItem) → inherits ItemName, ItemQty and adds its own field ItemCountry.

Therefore, the ExportItem table has ItemName, ItemQty, and ItemCountry.

Main knowledge to remember:

Tables in ServiceNow are hierarchical.

A child table inherits all fields and scripts from its parent table.

You can add extra fields only to the child table, but it always keeps the parent’s fields.

Reference: Table extension and classes (ServiceNow Docs)

pergunta: Which one of the following is the correct Link Type to select when creating a module which opens the Record Producer UI for a user rather than the ServiceNow form UI?

alternativas.explicacao:
When you create a module in ServiceNow that should open a Record Producer UI, you need to use a URL (from Arguments:) link type.

This is because Record Producers are accessed via a catalog URL (they live within the Service Catalog), not through a standard form view.
So instead of pointing to a table form, the module points directly to the Record Producer’s URL in the format:

catalog_item.do?sys_id=<record_producer_sys_id>

or

com.glideapp.servicecatalog_cat_item_view.do?v=1&sys_id=<sys_id>

This ensures users are redirected to the Record Producer UI — the catalog-based form designed for user-friendly record creation.

Main knowledge to remember:

Record Producers use the Service Catalog UI, not standard forms.

Use Link Type = URL (from Arguments:) and provide the proper catalog item URL.

The goal is to give users a guided form experience, not direct access to database records.

Reference:

- Create a module for a template (ServiceNow Docs)

- Invoke the Schedule page and view a calendar (ServiceNow Docs)

A custom table x_teddybear_project extends the Task table.
The following ACLs are configured:

Table ACL:

x_teddybear_project | read

Role required: itil

Field ACLs:

x_teddybear_project.field1 | read

No specific roles required (inherits table access)

x_teddybear_project.field2 | read

No field-level ACL defined

x_teddybear_project.field3 | read

Role required: admin

No other ACLs exist on this table or fields.

Which field or fields can a user with the itil role read?

alternativas.explicacao:
The correct answer is All fields except field3.

To understand why, we have to look at how ServiceNow processes Access Control Lists (ACLs) using a "top-down" approach, moving from the general (table level) to the specific (field level).

The ACL Evaluation Process

In ServiceNow, for a user to see a field, they must pass two gates:

Gate 1 (Table Level): Does the user have permission to see the table?

Gate 2 (Field Level): Does the user have permission to see the specific field?

Breaking Down the Access for the ITIL User

Table Access: The user has the itil role. Since the Table ACL for x_teddybear_project requires the itil role, the user passes Gate 1. They can now access the records in the table.

field1 Access: There is a field-level ACL, but it doesn't list any specific roles. In ServiceNow, if a field ACL exists without specific roles, it essentially inherits the table-level requirement. Since the user passed the table-level check, they can read field1.

field2 Access: There is no field-level ACL defined at all. When no field-level ACL exists, the system defaults to the table-level result. Since the user is allowed to read the table, they are granted access to all fields on that table that don't have their own specific restrictions. Therefore, they can read field2.

field3 Access: There is a specific field-level ACL that requires the admin role. This is an "explicit" restriction. Even though the ITIL user passed the table-level check, they do not have the admin role required by this specific field-level gate. Therefore, they cannot read field3.

Reference: Configure security (ServiceNow Docs)

pergunta:
What are the benefits of storing the majority of an Application’s server-side script logic in a Script Include?

a. This makes execution faster.

b. Only run when called from a script.

c. The script logic can be hidden when the Application is installed from the ServiceNow Store.

d. For some changes to application logic there is only one place to make edits.

alternativas.explicacao:
In ServiceNow, Script Includes are used to store reusable server-side logic. The correct benefits of storing the majority of an application’s server-side logic in a Script Include are:

Only run when called from a script

Script Includes do not execute automatically. They run only when another script explicitly calls them, which improves control and avoids unnecessary execution.

The script logic can be hidden when the Application is installed from the ServiceNow Store

Script Includes can be marked as protected, preventing customers from viewing or modifying the code after installation. This is especially important for applications distributed through the ServiceNow Store.

For some changes to application logic there is only one place to make edits

Centralizing logic in a Script Include improves maintainability and reuse. When business logic changes, developers update it in one location instead of multiple scripts.

Main takeaway:

Script Includes provide controlled execution, code protection, and centralized logic management.
They are a best practice for organizing server-side logic but do not guarantee faster performance.

Reference: Script includes (ServiceNow Docs)

alternativas.explicacao:
Breakdown Relations and Data Collection

In Performance Analytics, Breakdown Relations allow you to navigate through hierarchical data (like an organizational structure) by defining a relationship between two breakdown elements (e.g., Assigned To and Manager).

The Correct Answer When the Data Collector is executed.

Key Breakdown

Snapshot in Time: Performance Analytics is designed to capture a "snapshot" of data. When the Data Collector job runs, it queries the current state of the records (including the Assigned To and their Manager) and stores that specific relationship in the scores table.

Point-of-Collection: If a user’s manager changes after the data collector has finished its run, that change will not be reflected in the existing scores for that day. The system uses the relationship that was active at the exact moment the data was "collected."

Consistency: This ensures that historical trending remains accurate to what the organizational structure actually looked like on the day the data was recorded.

Timeline Page: Opens a timeline visualization, often used in Project Management or Change Management to see schedules.

Run a Report: Directly opens a specific report.

New Record: Opens a blank form to create a new entry in a table.

URL (from arguments:) : Allows you to link to an external website or a specific page within ServiceNow using a relative URL.

Single Record: Opens one specific, pre-defined record.
